rotations.explanation_text: Schedule feasibility: rotation_b is feasible; all operation dates fall inside the cited windows. This is calendar feasibility under statewide usual practice and cited NC State tables, not a field guarantee. Modeled water demand: under identical historical weather, rotation_b had more modeled unmet crop-water demand than rotation_a on average (165.0 mm vs 164.6 mm; mean paired difference 0.4 mm); lower in 0 and higher in 2 of 40 overlapping blocks. This is a screening indicator, not crop damage. Planned living cover: over the 3-year block the schedule has 334 more planned days with a living crop than rotation_a and less rainfall on days with low modeled living cover (1254.1 mm vs 2110.3 mm). This is an exposure proxy, not erosion or runoff. Trade-off: objectives point in different directions (lower than baseline: rainfall_low_cover_index_mm; higher: water_deficit_mm). No combined score is computed. Sensitivity: the direction of the modeled unmet crop-water demand comparison (higher) did not change across 24 parameter sets (storage, Kc, dates, residue, cover and initial-condition scenarios). Sensitivity: the direction of the rainfall falling on days with low modeled living cover comparison (lower) did not change across 24 parameter sets (storage, Kc, dates, residue, cover and initial-condition scenarios). Unfavorable weather blocks (largest increase in modeled unmet demand versus baseline): historical_2000_2002 (+15.9 mm), historical_1984_1986 (+0.6 mm), historical_2002_2004 (+0.0 mm). Not substantiated by this model: yield, profit, erosion or runoff, nitrogen or carbon credits, future outcomes, or field validity.

Sensitivity: the direction of the rainfall falling on days with low modeled living cover comparison (lower) did not change across 24 parameter sets (storage, Kc, dates, residue, cover and initial-condition scenarios). Unfavorable weather blocks (largest increase in modeled unmet demand versus baseline): historical_1985_1987 (+103.1 mm), historical_1984_1986 (+102.4 mm), historical_2021_2023 (+75.8 mm).
